questions.prompt: Which Russian leader was assassinated in 1881 by the group Narodnaya Volya?
questions.hint: He was known as the 'Tsar Liberator'.
questions.explanation: Alexander II was killed in 1881 by Narodnaya Volya, a revolutionary group, despite his reforms like emancipating the serfs in 1861.

questions.prompt: The element discovered in the Sun’s corona during an 1868 eclipse is ____.
questions.hint: It’s the second most abundant element in the universe.
questions.explanation: Helium was identified in the Sun’s corona by spectroscopy in 1868 by Pierre Janssen, before its earthly discovery in 1895.

questions.prompt: The novel 'One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest' was inspired by the author’s work in a ____ hospital.
questions.explanation: Ken Kesey wrote 'One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest' (1962) based on his experiences working in a psychiatric hospital, critiquing mental health care.

questions.prompt: Which country’s flag features a cedar tree at its center?
questions.explanation: Lebanon’s flag, adopted in 1943, displays a green cedar tree, symbolizing strength and eternity, between red and white stripes.

questions.prompt: Which Formula 1 driver won his first world championship at the age of 22?
questions.explanation: Sebastian Vettel won his first Formula 1 World Championship in 2010 at age 22, driving for Red Bull, the youngest champion then.

questions.prompt: The TV series 'The Wire' is primarily set in which U.S. city?
questions.explanation: 'The Wire' (2002-2008) is set in Baltimore, exploring its drug trade, education, and politics across five seasons.

questions.prompt: The painting 'The Last Supper' was commissioned for a monastery in which Italian city?
questions.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci painted 'The Last Supper' (1495-1498) for the Santa Maria delle Grazie monastery in Milan.

questions.prompt: Which artist’s album 'Thriller' became the best-selling album of all time?
questions.explanation: Michael Jackson’s 'Thriller' (1982) has sold over 66 million copies worldwide, making it the best-selling album ever.

questions.prompt: The ancient library of Alexandria was located in which modern-day country?
questions.explanation: The Library of Alexandria, a major center of learning in antiquity, was in Egypt, founded in the 3rd century BCE.

questions.prompt: The 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand sparked which global conflict?
questions.explanation: Archduke Franz Ferdinand’s assassination in Sarajevo in 1914 triggered World War I, drawing in global alliances.

questions.prompt: The scientist who proposed the heliocentric model of the solar system was ____.
questions.explanation: Nicolaus Copernicus published his heliocentric theory in 1543, asserting the Sun, not Earth, was the solar system’s center.

questions.prompt: The only country in the world named after a woman is ____.
questions.explanation: Saint Lucia, named after Saint Lucy of Syracuse, is the only sovereign country named for a woman, gaining independence in 1979.

questions.prompt: Which cricketer holds the record for the most Test match centuries?
questions.explanation: Sachin Tendulkar scored 51 Test centuries in his career (1989-2013), a record in international cricket.

questions.prompt: The artist who painted 'The Kiss' in 1907-1908 was from which country?
questions.explanation: Gustav Klimt, an Austrian, painted 'The Kiss' (1907-1908), a gold-leaf masterpiece of the Viennese Art Nouveau movement.

questions.prompt: The character Deadpool first appeared in which comic book publisher’s universe?
questions.explanation: Deadpool debuted in Marvel’s 'New Mutants' #98 (1991), created by Rob Liefeld and Fabian Nicieza, known for breaking the fourth wall.

questions.prompt: The 1929 Wall Street Crash marked the beginning of which economic event?
questions.explanation: The Wall Street Crash of October 1929 triggered the Great Depression, a global economic downturn lasting a decade.

questions.prompt: Which Russian novel features a character named Raskolnikov who commits a murder?
questions.explanation: Fyodor Dostoevsky’s 'Crime and Punishment' (1866) follows Raskolnikov, a student wrestling with guilt after murder.

questions.prompt: The world’s largest salt flat, Salar de Uyuni, is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Salar de Uyuni in Bolivia spans over 10,000 square kilometers, a vast salt flat formed from prehistoric lakes.

questions.prompt: The first modern Olympic Games to include women’s events were held in which year?
questions.explanation: The 1900 Paris Olympics were the first to include women, with events like tennis and golf, a milestone in sports history.

questions.prompt: Which rock band’s name is derived from a term for a UFO sighting?
questions.hint: It was formed by Dave Grohl.
questions.explanation: Foo Fighters, named after WWII pilots’ term for UFOs, was founded by Dave Grohl in 1994 post-Nirvana.

questions.prompt: The Dutch painter Hieronymus Bosch is best known for his triptych titled ____.
questions.hint: It’s a surreal vision of paradise and hell.
questions.explanation: Hieronymus Bosch’s 'The Garden of Earthly Delights' (circa 1490-1510) is a triptych depicting creation, sin, and damnation.

questions.prompt: The 1980s TV show 'Knight Rider' featured a talking car named ____.
questions.hint: It stands for 'Knight Industries Two Thousand'.
questions.explanation: 'Knight Rider' (1982-1986) starred David Hasselhoff with KITT, an AI-equipped Pontiac Trans Am.

questions.prompt: The first successful powered flight by the Wright brothers occurred in which U.S. state?
questions.explanation: The Wright brothers’ first powered flight took place on December 17, 1903, in Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

questions.prompt: The strongest acid known, fluoroantimonic acid, contains which element discovered in 1783?
questions.explanation: Fluoroantimonic acid, the strongest superacid, includes antimony (Sb), discovered in 1783, enhancing its corrosive power.

questions.prompt: The Pulitzer Prize-winning novel 'The Grapes of Wrath' is set during which historical event?
questions.explanation: John Steinbeck’s 'The Grapes of Wrath' (1939) depicts a family’s struggles during the Great Depression and Dust Bowl.

questions.prompt: The 1453 fall of which city marked the end of the Byzantine Empire?
questions.explanation: Constantinople fell to the Ottoman Turks in 1453, ending the Byzantine Empire and shifting power in the Eastern Mediterranean.

questions.prompt: The scientist who discovered penicillin in 1928 was ____.
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 when mold contaminated a petri dish, revolutionizing antibiotics.

questions.prompt: Which poet’s work inspired the musical 'Cats'?
questions.hint: It’s from 'Old Possum’s Book of Practical Cats'.
questions.explanation: T.S. Eliot’s 1939 poetry collection 'Old Possum’s Book of Practical Cats' inspired Andrew Lloyd Webber’s musical 'Cats' (1981).

questions.prompt: The Gobi Desert spans parts of which two countries?
questions.explanation: The Gobi Desert covers northern China and southern Mongolia, a vast arid region known for dinosaur fossils.

questions.prompt: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cup titles?
questions.explanation: Brazil has won the FIFA World Cup five times (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002), more than any other nation.

questions.prompt: The film 'Citizen Kane' is loosely based on the life of which newspaper magnate?
questions.explanation: Orson Welles’ 'Citizen Kane' (1941) mirrors William Randolph Hearst’s life, a powerful media tycoon, sparking controversy.

questions.prompt: The Impressionist painter Claude Monet was born in which country?
questions.explanation: Claude Monet, born in France in 1840, was a founder of Impressionism, known for works like 'Impression, Sunrise'.

questions.prompt: Which 1970s band’s name is inspired by a science fiction novel by Robert A. Heinlein?
questions.explanation: Jefferson Starship, formed in 1974, took its name partly from Heinlein’s 'Stranger in a Strange Land', succeeding Jefferson Airplane.

questions.prompt: The first Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded in 1901 to ____ for discovering X-rays.
questions.explanation: Wilhelm Röntgen received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901 for discovering X-rays in 1895, advancing medical imaging.

questions.prompt: The Magna Carta was signed by which English king?
questions.explanation: King John signed the Magna Carta in 1215 at Runnymede, a foundational document limiting royal power in England.

questions.prompt: The largest moon in our solar system belongs to which planet?
questions.explanation: Jupiter’s moon Ganymede is the largest in the solar system, bigger than Mercury, discovered by Galileo in 1610.

questions.prompt: The character Jay Gatsby is from a novel set during which decade?
questions.explanation: Jay Gatsby appears in 'The Great Gatsby' (1925) by F. Scott Fitzgerald, set in the Roaring Twenties, exploring the Jazz Age.

questions.prompt: Which European country has the most active volcanoes?
questions.explanation: Italy has the most active volcanoes in Europe, including Mount Etna, Vesuvius, and Stromboli, due to its tectonic setting.

questions.prompt: The Stanley Cup is awarded in which sport?
questions.explanation: The Stanley Cup, first awarded in 1893, is the championship trophy of the National Hockey League (NHL).

questions.prompt: The TV show 'Breaking Bad' follows a chemistry teacher turned drug lord named ____.
questions.explanation: 'Breaking Bad' (2008-2013) centers on Walter White, a teacher who becomes a methamphetamine kingpin after a cancer diagnosis.

questions.prompt: The sculpture 'David' by Michelangelo is housed in which Italian city?
questions.explanation: Michelangelo’s 'David' (1501-1504) resides in Florence’s Galleria dell’Accademia, a symbol of Renaissance art.

questions.prompt: The video game 'Pac-Man' was first released in which year?
questions.explanation: 'Pac-Man', created by Toru Iwatani for Namco, debuted in 1980, becoming an iconic arcade game.

questions.prompt: The currency of Brazil is the ____.
questions.explanation: The Brazilian Real (BRL) became Brazil’s currency in 1994, stabilizing its economy after hyperinflation.

questions.prompt: The ancient city of Carthage was located in which modern-day country?
questions.explanation: Carthage, a major power in antiquity, is in modern-day Tunisia, near Tunis, and was Rome’s rival in the Punic Wars.

questions.prompt: The human body’s largest organ by surface area is the ____.
questions.hint: It protects you from the outside world.
questions.explanation: The skin is the body’s largest organ, covering about 1.5-2 square meters, serving as a barrier and regulator.

questions.prompt: The longest river in South America is the ____.
questions.explanation: The Amazon River, stretching over 6,575 km, is South America’s longest, vital to the rainforest ecosystem.

questions.prompt: Which tennis player was the first to win all four Grand Slam titles in a single year?
questions.explanation: Don Budge achieved the first calendar-year Grand Slam in 1938, winning all four major tennis titles.

questions.prompt: The director of 'The Lord of the Rings' trilogy hails from which country?
questions.explanation: Peter Jackson, from New Zealand, directed 'The Lord of the Rings' trilogy (2001-2003), filmed in his home country.

questions.prompt: The painting 'Girl with a Pearl Earring' is often compared to the 'Mona Lisa' and was created by ____.
questions.explanation: Johannes Vermeer’s 'Girl with a Pearl Earring' (circa 1665) is a Dutch masterpiece, admired for its enigmatic subject.

questions.prompt: The animated series 'The Simpsons' is set in a fictional town named ____.
questions.explanation: 'The Simpsons', launched in 1989, takes place in the ambiguous Springfield, a satirical take on American life.

questions.prompt: The inventor of the telephone, credited in 1876, was ____.
questions.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone in 1876, a breakthrough in communication technology.

questions.prompt: The Treaty of Versailles, ending World War I, was signed in which year?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Versailles was signed on June 28, 1919, formally ending World War I and imposing terms on Germany.

questions.prompt: The deepest part of the world’s oceans is located in which trench?
questions.explanation: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean reaches a depth of about 11,000 meters at the Challenger Deep.

questions.prompt: The Bronte sister who wrote 'Wuthering Heights' used which pseudonym?
questions.explanation: Emily Bronte published 'Wuthering Heights' (1847) as Ellis Bell, concealing her gender in a male-dominated era.
